newsitem.title: UK: Milan/Rome air cargo hubs need to be urgently developed.
newsitem.headline: Milan/Rome air cargo hubs need to be urgently developed.

text.p: Air cargo hubs at Milan and Rome need to be developed soon if Italy is to compete with major north European airports, industry leaders said in interviews here.

Giordano Angelini who is responsible for transport policy in the PDS political party and Paolo Becchetti, vice president of the parliamentary transport committee said Italian airports need to match the services provided by their northern European counterparts.

"The development of the hubs at Milano-Malpensa and Rome-Fiumicino is imperative if the cargo city of Malpensa 2000 is to fulfull its potential and compete with the major airports of North Europe (such as Amsterdam, Frankfurt, Zurich, London and Paris)," Angelini said.

"These airports are taking away much of our aircargo traffic with their trucking Systems. Of the 74 percent of Italian exports that come from northern Italy, 70 percent flies from non-Italian airports," he added.

"The geography of Italy makes it essential that Rome's Fiumicino airport is fully developed to provide an efficient cargo hub for the central-southern area where 26 percent of the national manufactured articles are generated," Angelini said.

"The advantage gained by cargo flying by air should not be wasted on the ground. And as Italy handles valuable cargo with high transport, services should be reliable, faster and of a higher quality," Becchetti said.

"Although Turin-Caselle airport is able to carry cargo for Alitalia, this is now being transferred to Malpensa which is now under construction," Bacchetti added. - Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+5017
